title: Inject a fake clock instead of comparing against real DateTime.now() in completion/restore timing assertions
why: Both assertions pin correctness to a 5-second window measured against the real wall clock at assertion time, rather than the FakeLocalDayClock/DateTimeFactory override the codebase already provides and uses correctly elsewhere (e.g. epic_08_gamification_test.dart Story 8.2). On a slow or contended CI runner, a stall of more than 5 seconds between the write and the assertion — plausible for a cold Drift/sqlite3 open — flakes the test for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
recommendation: Install a FakeLocalDayClock (or equivalent) before the write and assert equality/near-equality against the fake's fixed instant, matching the pattern already used in epic_08_gamification_test.dart Story 8.2.
acceptance_criteria: Both assertions compare against a fixed/fake clock value, not a DateTime.now()/DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() call made at assertion time

corrections: epic_03_learning_cycle_test.dart evidence line should be 119, not 118 — the quoted text begins one line after the cited line number.
